title: Smooth constant-coefficient assertions imply open-immersion lower-shriek assertions
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], r a prime, and R = ULift(Z/rZ). Assume that for every smooth separated finite-type curve g:C → Spec k of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the constant R-module sheaf with value R/(r) [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] satisfies all eight assertions [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. Then for every smooth curve f:X → Spec k with the same conventions and every open immersion j:U → X [def-weil-open-immersion], j_! of the constant R-module sheaf with value R/(r) on U satisfies all eight assertions on X [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Empty, disconnected and zero-dimensional curves are allowed.

source.place: Lemma 59.83.7, proof: disjoint smooth components, empty or dense intersection, and dense-open localization

proof.text: Finite type over k makes X Noetherian, hence gives finitely many irreducible components. Smooth curve local rings are normal domains. Distinct irreducible components through one point would give distinct minimal primes in its local domain, impossible. Thus the components are disjoint. Each is closed and has closed complement, the finite union of the other components, so each is also open. The component inclusion is consequently both open and closed, hence finite. Each component is a smooth curve over k.

On each component C the pullback of j is an open immersion. If its image is empty, extension by zero is zero, whose cohomology vanishes and whose comparisons are isomorphisms. Otherwise its image is dense because C is irreducible. Apply the hypothesis H to C; the constant finite coefficient sheaf is constructible and annihilated by r. Its restriction is canonically the constant coefficient sheaf on the pullback open. Apply dense-open prime-torsion localization to obtain the assertions for extension by zero. A zero-dimensional component has no proper nonempty open, so the nonempty case is the identity comparison and needs no separate zero-dimensional cohomology theorem.

Transfer each component extension-by-zero sheaf by its finite open-and-closed inclusion. Finite pushforward preserves the assertions; when using the abelian-sheaf formulation, forget the finite-field module structure. The underlying abelian sheaf of the module direct image is canonically the abelian direct image, since sections and restriction maps coincide; this is not an equivalence of finite-field modules with abelian groups. The definitions of the eight assertions use these underlying abelian sheaves. The canonical comparisons commute with inverse image and cohomology maps, and constructibility and torsion hypotheses agree for these finite prime-field sheaves. Affineness and properness of X pass to its open-and-closed components. Component projections preserve primary and invertible torsion hypotheses, so each conditional assertion applies to every summand with the required hypotheses. On the disjoint component cover these pushforwards form a finite direct sum canonically isomorphic to j_! of the constant coefficient sheaf on U. For two summands use the split short exact sequence from the first summand to the sum to the second summand, and iterate curve devissage. The isomorphism is induced by the component restrictions and therefore commutes with field-extension pullback and open restriction. This proves all eight conditional assertions with the original comparison maps. When X is empty the sum has no summands and is zero.

lean.statement:
theorem smoothConstantLowerShriekAssertions_of_constant
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (r : ℕ) [Fact r.Prime]
    (H : ∀ {C : Scheme.{u}} (g : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve g] [Smooth g],
      IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r)) g
        (Etale.constantModSheaf (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r)) C r))
    {X U : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f] [Smooth f]
    (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] :
    IsCurve.Assertions (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r)) f
      ((Etale.openImmersionLowerShriek
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r))) j).obj
        (Etale.constantModSheaf (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod r)) U r))
